What this map proves, and what it does not

These cases trace named counterparties where public sources support a connection. Many supplier revenues, bank exposures and model-lab cash flows are not disclosed by customer. Missing links remain unknown. A supply chain has successive payments; a financing loop has additional investment, credit, guarantees or equity incentives linking participants back together.

Amounts retain their original scope and date. “Up to,” “committed,” “facility,” “guarantee,” “framework,” “paid” and “recognized revenue” describe different things. Do not add them together. Two disclosed contracts do not prove the same dollar moved through both. Supplier relationships do not establish a verified payment amount. Ant is interpreted as Anthropic; OpenAI and Anthropic are private companies included as counterparties, outside the 100 public-company financial universe.

Valuation and debt method

The hidden-champion screen remains a business and relative-price screen. Valuation is an additional check, not a new claim that the candidate is undervalued. Debt is not the same as total liabilities. Operating leases, purchase commitments, guarantees and project financing can matter beyond reported borrowings. Negative net debt means cash exceeds the captured debt; it does not prove every obligation is covered.

Research method, limitations and scenario evidence

The analysis starts with each company’s economic role, then asks how demand, competition, pricing and capital needs change under each scenario. Ratings from −3 to +3 are authored relative-position judgments; they are not outputs of a financial forecast. Top selections are editorial priorities. Companies with similar ratings are not precisely ranked against one another.

Hidden-champion eligibility adds observed financial and market gates to the scenario rating. A company may pass the screen yet face substitution, acquisition-distorted growth, one-off profits, stock-based compensation or an expensive valuation. We have not modelled debt maturities, fair value, consensus expectations or portfolio suitability across all 100 companies. No probability is assigned to these scenarios.

The strict stock screen requires underperformance both over one year and since the first common trading day of 2023. The recent-laggard option uses only one year. Listings without a comparable 2023 window and major restructuring/spin-off cases (Nebius, Western Digital, Jacobs) are excluded from the strict window. US-listed foreign shares use a US benchmark, which introduces regional and currency differences. A negative FCF figure can reflect productive expansion. Missing or older evidence prevents a company passing the screen, but does not automatically make it a loser.

Sources support observed conditions and business channels. Future outcomes, spending paths, ratings and picks are our conditional analysis. The IEA’s 2026 central projection is approximately 950 TWh of global data-centre electricity use in 2030, not a stock-market forecast. Scenario 3 combines a returns reset with deployment constraints; geopolitics, regulation, recession and supply disruptions could alter any of the three.

05 / READ THE NUMBERS PROPERLY

Traceable numbers.
Clear boundaries.

What this universe represents

100 selected public companies with exposure to AI platforms, chips, manufacturing, networking, electrical systems, energy, cooling, facilities and software. Selection balances major buyers with upstream and downstream suppliers. It is not the 100 largest companies or an investment ranking.

Sector assignments and potential benefit channels are editorial interpretations of each company's business. Inclusion does not mean AI is its main revenue source or that future profits are guaranteed. Links are schematic roles, not verified supplier contracts.

What “making money” means

Net income is reported accounting profit or loss. Free cash flow is operating cash flow less cash capital expenditure when comparable components are available. Company-reported FCF is labeled where used and may include different adjustments.

Positive net income with negative FCF means accounting profit alongside cash use after investment. Negative FCF can fund expansion; it does not by itself mean operating failure. Stock returns are shown separately in Hidden champions; they do not measure operating profitability.

Periods, currencies and freshness

Most SEC records use trailing twelve months (TTM), calculated as the latest fiscal year plus current year-to-date minus the comparable prior year-to-date. Where this cannot be reconstructed, the latest available annual period is used. Other company releases use the quarter or half-year explicitly shown.

Amounts stay in their reported currencies. We do not add amounts across companies or currencies. Margins use matching periods. Older periods receive a freshness label. This is a saved research snapshot; there is no automatic refresh.

Sources and missing data

Financials come from SEC structured filings and company investor-relations releases checked for this edition. Quanta Computer uses a clearly labeled secondary-source summary where the issuer download was unavailable. Company details link to sources and expose the source periods and formula components. SEC structured data can lag a newer earnings release, especially for foreign issuers.

A dash means unavailable or not safely comparable, never zero. Missing cash data is excluded from cash classifications and the scatterplot. Accounting policies, asset sales, acquisitions, investment gains and share-based pay can distort comparisons. REIT free cash flow differs from FFO/AFFO.

SEC data documentation

How the hidden-champion screen works

The screen requires reported revenue growth of at least 10% year on year, positive net income, positive free cash flow, financial period ending within 180 days of this snapshot, and share-price returns below its benchmark both over one year and since the first common trading day of 2023. Major spin-off/restructuring cases and shorter listings do not pass the strict multi-year test. Missing, older or incompatible evidence does not pass. Growth uses the same reported currency and duration; the basis is shown for each company. Acquisitions and currency movements can affect reported growth.

Prices are a saved Yahoo Finance historical-data snapshot, using split-adjusted closing prices and excluding dividends. Stock and benchmark returns use identical available trading dates. S&P 500 is used for USD-listed shares, KOSPI for Korean shares, Taiwan Weighted for Taiwan shares, EURO STOXX 50 for euro listings, and SMI for Swiss listings. Benchmark choice affects results. This measures relative stock performance, not how much AI is priced in; it does not measure valuation, analyst expectations or investor awareness.
